title: Selected answer differs from submitted answer
description: On Question 2 of the MCQ assessment, selecting Option B ('O(n log n)') causes the client-side radio input or form payload to submit Option C ('O(n²)') instead of the selected Option B, resulting in an unexpected answer mismatch on the results page.
steps_to_reproduce: Select Option B ('O(n log n)') and confirm the radio is checked
Complete or proceed to submit the assessment
Inspect Question 2 on the results page
expected: The results page should display the candidate's selected answer as Option B.
actual: The submitted answer recorded and displayed on the results page is Option C (or A).

title: Negative marking is calculated incorrectly
description: The assessment instructions state that each correct answer awards +4 marks and each incorrect answer deducts a -1 mark penalty. However, the scoring engine calculates negative marks as -4 marks per incorrect answer instead of -1.
steps_to_reproduce: Submit an assessment with 2 correct answers, 1 incorrect answer, and 1 unattempted question
expected: The net MCQ score should be (2 * 4) - (1 * 1) = 7 marks.
actual: The scoring engine computes (2 * 4) - (1 * 4) = 4 marks, deducting a 4-point penalty per wrong answer.

title: Duplicate submission changes assessment results
description: Submitting the MCQ assessment multiple times with the same candidate identifier or submission ID alters the score accumulator instead of returning an idempotent, unchanged result.
steps_to_reproduce: Submit an MCQ assessment and note the initial score on the results page
Click the browser back button and submit the form again (or replay the POST submission request)
Observe the updated score on the results page
expected: Assessment submissions must be idempotent; duplicate submissions should not alter the score.
actual: The duplicate submission increments the score accumulator or mutates the assessment result.

title: Hidden test cases are ignored during scoring
description: The coding evaluation scoring engine calculates candidate points solely from visible public test cases, ignoring hidden edge-case test cases in the score calculation.
steps_to_reproduce: Enter a hardcoded or partial solution that passes only the 2 public test cases and fails hidden edge cases (e.g., negative numbers)
Click Submit Solution and view the results
expected: The solution should receive 50/100 points because only 2 out of 4 test cases passed.
actual: The solution receives 100/100 points because hidden test cases are omitted from scoring.

title: Previous submission results are reused
description: When a candidate submits a second coding solution for the same problem, the backend coding evaluation handler reuses the cached evaluation verdict and score from their previous submission instead of executing the new code.
steps_to_reproduce: Submit an incorrect solution (e.g., 'def find_target_pair(nums, target): return []') and note the 0/100 score
Replace the code in the editor with a fully correct solution
expected: The second submission should execute the new code and award 100/100 points with an Accepted verdict.
actual: The second submission displays the cached results from the first submission (0/100, Wrong Answer).
